final_candidates.decision_summary: High EVEscape and strong structure compatibility with acceptable sequence plausibility make this the safest escape-while-viable substitution.
Highest predicted escape and best structural compatibility; zero evolutionary frequency is a concern but outweighed by structural support.
Good escape and solid structure compatibility; low sequence prior adds some replication-fitness uncertainty but not disqualifying.

stop_reason.detail: Available evidence already produced a stable Top-3 and the tool-call budget is exhausted; additional rounds would not change the final mutations.

history.rationale: Located in the Sa antigenic site; introducing a larger polar residue may alter antibody recognition while likely maintaining surface compatibility.
No evidence collected this round; retained based on initial positioning in an antigenically relevant HA head region.
Good escape (0.743) with solid structure compatibility (0.912); low PLM prior is a caution but not disqualifying.

No evidence collected this round; retained for charge-change potential at a surface-exposed position.
Highest escape (0.901) and best structure delta (0.973); low sequence/evolution priors are outweighed by strong structural support.
Surface-exposed Sa-site substitution that changes side-chain chemistry and may escape strain-specific antibodies.
No evidence collected this round; retained as a conservative glycosylation-site-modifying candidate.
Strong PLM plausibility and moderate escape, but missing structure score adds replication-fitness uncertainty.
Aromatic-to-polar change in a surface antigenic loop may reduce antibody recognition while preserving loop flexibility.
No evidence collected this round; retained as an aromatic-to-basic substitution at a potentially exposed epitope position.
Moderate escape and structure compatibility, but very low sequence-model support keeps it mid-pool.
Charged substitution at the Sa/Ca1 interface adds electrostatic variation to a known antigenic region.
No evidence collected this round; retained for charge-change potential near the receptor-binding region.
Very poor structure compatibility (0.065) signals severe folding disruption, rejecting the modest evolutionary support.

history.rationale: Sb antigenic site residue; replacing glutamine with histidine alters polar interactions and may lower antibody binding.

history.rationale: Sb-site substitution with a larger polar side chain can modify the exposed epitope without major hydrophobic disruption.

High EVEscape (0.822) plus strong structure compatibility (0.927) and acceptable PLM (0.247) make it the safest escape-while-folded candidate.
Loss of a polar side chain in the Sb region may remove a key antibody contact while retaining local backbone flexibility.
No evidence collected this round; retained as a conservative deglycosylation candidate.
Moderate escape (0.730) with good structure (0.834) and the best evolutionary/PLM support among the pool.

No evidence collected this round; retained for possible epitope-disrupting acidic substitution.
Decent structure compatibility but only moderate escape and very low sequence/evolution priors.
